page: Microsoft Azure E16-8ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine within the Edsv6 series, tailored for architectures requiring substantial memory allocations per processor core. Hardware specifications center on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 4 physical cores and 8 dedicated vCPUs operating at speeds up to 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture incorporates 260 MB of L3 cache and supports Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) as well as AVX-512 vector instructions. Memory capacity stands at 128 GB, establishing an elevated 16 GB of RAM per vCPU. The server bundles 945 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage, while omitting onboard GPUs and complimentary public IPv4 addressing.

In synthetic and execution benchmarks, the instance demonstrates distinct single-threaded strengths alongside balanced multi-threaded throughput. Single-core performance ranks in the top quartile, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2154.0 and gzip compression throughput reaching 31.38 GB/sec. Text processing and lightweight LLM token generation also achieve strong tiers. In contrast, multi-core benchmarks such as stress-ng (7989.66) and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression align with average baseline metrics for 8-vCPU environments. Memory bandwidth benchmarks deliver 64.02 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 43.34 GB/sec for writes, accompanied by PassMark database operational metrics and Redis throughput exceeding 11.8 million operations per second.

From an architectural and cost-efficiency perspective, the constrained ratio of 8 vCPUs against 128 GB of RAM creates clear resource tradeoffs. For highly parallel compute tasks or massive continuous rendering, the low physical core count represents a throughput ceiling. However, in environments governed by per-core software licensing, such as commercial relational database management systems, this configuration maximizes available memory and cache per licensed core. The bundled 945 GB NVMe SSD provides local high-throughput scratch space without requiring additional network storage overhead. Consequently, the instance is well suited for in-memory data stores, Redis caching layers, ETL intermediate processing, and medium-scale transactional databases.
description: Microsoft Azure E16-8ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Edsv6 series designed for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz, the instance allocates 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores and features 260 MB of L3 cache alongside AMX and AVX-512 instruction support. The server provides 128 GB of system memory, yielding an expansive 16 GB of RAM per vCPU, and includes 945 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark results show strong single-threaded performance, including top-quartile Geekbench single-core scores and gzip compression throughput, while multi-core compute and memory bandwidth maintain steady mid-tier execution. The constrained core count limits dense parallel scaling, making the instance less cost-effective for pure compute-bound batch jobs, but highly cost-efficient when licensing costs favor lower core counts paired with large memory footprints. It is best suited for in-memory databases, Redis caches, and data analytics pipelines.
